license.adaptation_notice: Faithful editable transcription of the official CCC2020 CC BY3.0 publication, article26 pp26:1--26:13. One structured-Turing-hardness-to-circuit-lower-bound theme: introductory Theorems1/2, complete Section2 definitions/prerequisites3--6, complete Section3 Theorems7/8 author proofs, and complete Section4 Lemma9/Theorem10 full author proofs, including both simulations, padding construction, interval Claim and its full argument, robustly-often dichotomy, small hard-instance extraction and hard-query concatenation. All24 original bibliography entries retained. Parametric honest and natural are separate incomparable author conditions, both required only on correctly answered prefixes; their exact definitions and separate proof routes retained. No claim of a consequence for unrestricted/general Turing reductions, whose question remains open in original Section5. External standard diagonalization/Karp-Lipton/robust-simulation prerequisites and Gutfreund-Shaltiel-TaShma result remain at original author citation boundary without recursive proof. Original printed exponents/indices and wording retained without mathematical repair, including interval induction nprime_(j+1)=r(n_j), Claim strict/non-strict signs, first-disjunct T(n)=poly(r(n))n^s1(r(n)), and parameter s2 in failure-formula construction. Authors retain mathematical responsibility. No native source was provided by official page; formal PDF/text faithfully transcribed. No figures required. Root handles compilation/database/publication.

standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Original author Karp-Lipton/Meyer[19] and Gutfreund-Shaltiel-TaShma[12] uses and stated three-instance guarantee retained; no recursion into prior proofs.

core_obligations: Preserve distinct parametric-honest/natural conditions and correctly answered query-prefix restriction.
Retain complete parametric-honest proof, including all-YES simulation, hard-instance extraction and concatenation.
Retain complete natural proof, both thresholds, SAT padding, interval induction, robustly-often cases and final hard-query argument.
Group the two routes and MKtP test case once; do not claim unrestricted-Turing-hardness consequences.
difficulty_reason: The authors turn failure of a simulated SAT reduction into hard truth tables. The natural-reduction route couples two different parameter thresholds, padding-created long intervals and robustly-often indirect diagonalization to ensure that finding a failed instance costs far less than the circuit hardness extracted. These are explicit nonroutine structural mechanisms.
